answer: A farm's clones share one operator, so attack the sharing: at unpredictable moments, every identity is summoned at once to tend its own plot in a shared simulation, coaxing a different crop across a ridge before a storm lands — ten continuous minutes of unrelated decisions no script can pre-stage, because the weather is dealt live. One gardener works one garden easily, velvet-gloved and attentive; a thousand clones need a thousand simultaneous hands, since one operator can steer only one plot at a time and the rest wilt in public. Presence that cannot be queued or batched cannot be farmed.
